MCQs.question: Which part of the body is the control centre of the nervous system?
What do we call materials that let some light pass through but scatter it?
In which unit is the intensity of sound measured?
Which of these diseases can spread from one person to another?
What is the role of decomposers in a food web?
MCQs.answer: d) They break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil

b) They carry energy from the Sun to plants
c) They make food using sunlight

MCQs.question: Why can no one hear a sound made in outer space?
MCQs.answer: a) There is no air or other material for sound to travel through
options: a) There is no air or other material for sound to travel through
b) Sound is too fast to hear there

MCQs.answer: c) It teaches the body's defences to recognise and fight the germs
options: a) It works as a pain reliever
b) It kills all the germs in the air
c) It teaches the body's defences to recognise and fight the germs
d) It cures the disease immediately

MCQs.question: Which of these materials breaks down naturally and returns to the soil?
Which of these objects will be attracted by a magnet?
After a fast race, Rani finds that her pulse is much higher than before. What is the best reason?
MCQs.answer: b) Her heart pumps blood faster to bring more oxygen to her muscles
options: a) Her skin needs less blood
b) Her heart pumps blood faster to bring more oxygen to her muscles

MCQs.question: In a food chain, grass is eaten by rabbits and rabbits are eaten by foxes. If all the rabbits suddenly disappear, what will most likely happen to the foxes?
MCQs.answer: b) They may starve for lack of food
options: a) They will become herbivores overnight
b) They may starve for lack of food
c) They will have more food
d) They will stop needing energy

MCQs.question: A factory in Taleemabad pours its waste into a river. What is the most likely effect on the fish living there?
MCQs.answer: c) The fish may fall ill
options: a) The fish will stop needing air
b) The fish will grow faster
c) The fish may fall ill
d) The water will become cleaner

Jojo shines a torch on a wall and wants the darkest shadow. Which object should he place in front of the torch?
Gul Rukh strikes a steel glass first softly and then very hard. What will she notice?
MCQs.answer: b) The sound is louder because the waves have a larger amplitude
options: b) The sound is louder because the waves have a larger amplitude
c) The sound is softer because the waves are smaller
d) The sound stays the same

MCQs.question: Rani places two bar magnets on a table with their north poles facing each other and slides one towards the other. What happens?
MCQs.answer: a) They push each other away

Draw and Label.answer: A drawing of the human respiratory system with labels: nose, windpipe, left lung, right lung, voice box, diaphragm, throat.

Draw and Label.answer: A circle showing the Earth cut open with labels: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.

Logical Reasoning.question: Aisha puts a spoonful of sugar in a glass of water and stirs it. The sugar seems to disappear. She then leaves a little of this sweet water in a dish in the sun for some days and sees white grains in the dish.

questions.question: Why did the sugar seem to disappear when Aisha stirred it in the water?
questions.answer: The sugar dissolved and broke into tiny particles spread through the water, so it could not be seen, but it was still there.

points.text: States that the sugar dissolved or broke into tiny particles in the water
States that the sugar is still there, only not visible

questions.question: What are the white grains in the dish, and why did they appear?
questions.answer: They are sugar. The water dried up (evaporated) in the sun and left the sugar behind.

points.text: Identifies the grains as sugar
Explains that the water dried up or evaporated, leaving the sugar

questions.question: Is dissolving sugar in water a physical or a chemical change? Give a reason.
questions.answer: Physical change, because no new substance is formed and the sugar can be got back.

points.text: Names physical change
Gives a reason: no new substance formed or the change can be reversed

Logical Reasoning.question: Bilal puts two iron nails in two jars. One jar has plain water and the other has salty water. He leaves both jars for a week and looks at the nails each day.

questions.question: What will Bilal see on the nails after some days?
questions.answer: The nails will turn orange-brown because rust forms on them.

points.text: States that rust forms or the nails turn orange-brown

questions.question: In which jar will the nail rust faster, and why?
questions.answer: The jar with salty water, because salt makes rusting faster.

points.text: Names the salty water jar
Gives the reason that salt speeds up rusting

questions.question: Why is rusting called a chemical change?
questions.answer: Because a new substance with different properties is formed from the iron, and it cannot be easily reversed.

points.text: States that a new substance is formed
Mentions it is different from the iron or cannot be reversed easily

Logical Reasoning.question: Hira shines a torch at a wall in a dim room. She holds a clear plastic sheet in front of the light and sees a faint shadow. She then holds a thick cardboard sheet in front of the light and sees a dark shadow.

questions.question: Why is the shadow of the clear plastic sheet faint?
questions.answer: The plastic sheet is transparent, so it lets most of the light pass through.

points.text: Says the sheet is transparent
Says most light passes through it

questions.question: Why is the shadow of the cardboard dark?
questions.answer: Cardboard is opaque, so it blocks the light and no light passes through.

points.text: Says the cardboard is opaque
Says it blocks the light

questions.question: Hira now holds a frosted plastic cup in front of the light. What kind of shadow will she see and why?
questions.answer: A shadow darker than the clear sheet but lighter than the cardboard, because a translucent object lets only some light through.

points.text: States the shadow is in between faint and dark
Gives the reason that it is translucent and lets some light pass and scatters it

Brief Answers.question: Name the three main parts of the circulatory system and state what the heart does.
Brief Answers.answer: The three parts are the heart, the blood vessels and the blood. The heart works like a pump and pushes blood around the body.

points.text: Names the heart
Names the blood vessels
Names the blood
States that the heart is a pump / pumps blood around the body

Brief Answers.question: Define pollution and name its three main forms.
Brief Answers.answer: Pollution is the introduction of harmful materials into the environment. Its three main forms are air pollution, water pollution and land pollution.

points.text: Defines pollution as harmful substances added to / dirtying the environment
Names air pollution
Names water pollution
Names land pollution

Brief Answers.question: Define transparent, translucent and opaque objects.
Brief Answers.answer: Transparent objects let light pass through easily so we can see clearly through them. Translucent objects let some light pass through but scatter it, so things look blurry. Opaque objects do not let any light pass through.

points.text: Transparent: allows light to pass through easily / can see clearly
Translucent: allows some light, scatters it, things look blurry
Opaque: allows no light to pass / blocks light

Brief Answers.question: Explain two jobs of the skeletal system.
Brief Answers.answer: The skeletal system supports our body so we can stand straight. It also helps us move, and it protects organs like the heart and lungs.

points.text: First correct job given (support / helps us stand straight / gives the body a framework)
Explains the first job in a sentence (Explains the second job in a sentence)
Second correct job given (helps movement / protects internal organs)

Brief Answers.question: Explain how vaccines protect us from diseases like polio and COVID-19.
Brief Answers.answer: A vaccine puts a safe part of the germ into the body. This teaches the immune system to recognise the germ. If the real germ enters later, the body can fight it before it makes us very ill.

points.text: Vaccine gives a safe / harmless part of the germ
Teaches the immune system to recognise the germ (Body can fight the real germ in the future)

Brief Answers.question: Explain how a food web is different from a food chain.
Brief Answers.answer: A food chain is a single straight line showing who eats whom. A food web is made of many food chains that overlap and connect, because one animal or plant can be part of several chains.

points.text: Food chain is one single line / sequence of feeding
Food web is many food chains joined together (One living thing can belong to more than one chain in a web)

Brief Answers.question: Explain the difference between conductors and insulators. Give one example of each.
Brief Answers.answer: A conductor lets electric current flow through it easily, for example a copper wire or a coin. An insulator does not let current flow through it, for example wood or plastic.

points.text: Conductor allows electric current to flow easily
Insulator does not allow current to flow
A correct example of a conductor (A correct example of an insulator)

Brief Answers.question: A park has many fallen leaves. What would happen to the leaves and to the soil if there were no microorganisms? Give reasons.
Brief Answers.answer: The leaves would pile up and would not be broken down. Decomposition would stop, so nutrients would not return to the soil. The soil would become poor and new plants would not grow well.

points.text: Leaves would not break down / would pile up
Reason: microorganisms are the ones that decompose dead plants
Nutrients would not go back into the soil
New plants would not grow well

Brief Answers.question: Is burning a piece of wood a physical change or a chemical change? Give a reason.
Brief Answers.answer: Burning wood is a chemical change. New substances like black ash and smoke are formed that were not there before, and the wood cannot be changed back.

points.text: Says chemical change
Reason: new substances (ash, smoke, gases) are formed
Reason: the change cannot be reversed / wood is not the same material any more
Mentions heat or light given out during burning (combustion)

Brief Answers.question: A child ties a string around the middle of a bar magnet and hangs it in the air. The magnet slowly stops moving and points in one direction. Why does this happen?
Brief Answers.answer: The Earth acts like a giant magnet and has its own magnetic force. This force acts on the small magnet, so the magnet's north pole turns towards Earth's north and its south pole towards the south.

points.text: The Earth behaves like a giant magnet
Earth's magnetic force acts on the hanging magnet
The magnet lines up so its north pole faces north and south pole faces south

Long Question.question: Explain how a virus like the coronavirus can reach a healthy child and how masks, handwashing and vaccines help to stop it.
Long Question.answer: The coronavirus mainly travels in tiny droplets in the air when an infected child coughs or sneezes, and also through touching surfaces with germs on them. Masks block the droplets, handwashing removes germs from hands, and vaccines teach the immune system to fight the virus. Together these actions lower the chance of catching the disease.

points.text: Virus travels in airborne droplets from coughs or sneezes
Germs can also be picked up by touching infected surfaces or through close contact
Masks block / reduce the droplets reaching nose and mouth
Handwashing with soap and water removes germs from hands
Vaccines train the immune system to fight the virus

Long Question.question: Explain how the heart and lungs work together to help our body when we run in a race.
Long Question.answer: When we run, our muscles need more oxygen. We breathe harder so the lungs take in more oxygen and fill the blood with it. The heart beats more quickly and pumps the oxygen-rich blood through the blood vessels to the muscles. This is why our pulse rate goes up after exercise. Together they give the muscles the energy boost they need.

points.text: Muscles need extra oxygen during exercise
Breathing becomes heavy; the lungs fill the blood with oxygen
The heart beats more quickly and pumps more blood
Blood travels through blood vessels carrying oxygen to the muscles
Pulse rate rises / both work harder as a team

Long Question.question: Explain why dissolving sugar in water and melting ice are physical changes, and how each of these changes can be reversed.
Long Question.answer: In both changes no new substance is formed. When sugar dissolves, it breaks into tiny particles that are still sugar, so the water only becomes sweet. If the water evaporates, the sugar appears again. When ice melts, a solid changes into a liquid but it is still water. Putting the water in a freezer turns it back into ice.

points.text: A physical change does not form a new substance
Sugar breaks into tiny particles that are still sugar
Sugar can be got back by evaporating the water
Melting changes solid to liquid but it is still water
Liquid water can be frozen back into ice

Long Question.question: In a field, a food chain is grass, grasshopper, mouse, snake and hawk. Suppose all the snakes are removed from the field. Explain what would happen to the other living things and why.
Long Question.answer: The mice would not be eaten by snakes, so their number would grow. More mice would eat more grasshoppers, so grasshoppers would become fewer. The hawk would lose an important food source and might starve unless it finds other food. The flow of energy in the chain would be disturbed and the balance of the ecosystem would break.

points.text: Mice are no longer eaten by snakes so they increase
More mice eat more grasshoppers so grasshoppers decrease
Hawk loses food and may starve / have to find other food
The flow of energy in the chain is disturbed
The balance of the ecosystem is upset

Long Question.question: A child joins a battery, a bulb and two wires but the bulb does not light up. Explain what could be wrong and how the child can make the bulb glow.
Long Question.answer: For a bulb to glow, the battery, wires and bulb must form a complete closed loop so the current can flow. The child should check for a gap such as a loose wire or an open switch and fix it. They should also check that the battery is joined the right way round, with positive and negative terminals connected properly. If a material like wood is in the loop, it must be replaced with a conductor like a metal wire or paper clip, because wood does not let current pass.

points.text: The circuit must be a complete closed loop for current to flow
A break such as a loose wire or open switch makes an open circuit and stops current
Reconnect / close the gap to complete the loop
Check the battery is connected correctly (positive and negative terminals) and is not dead
An insulator such as wood or plastic in the loop does not allow current; use a conductor instead
